newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines Central Bank cuts overnight rates.
newsitem.headline: Philippines Central Bank cuts overnight rates.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank said on Tuesday it had cut its overnight rates by 0.25 percentage point each with immediate effect.
Its overnight lending rate is now at 13.0 percent from 13.25 percent; and its borrowing rate at 10.5 percent from 10.75 percent.
Money market dealers said the Central Bank had to move its rates downwards after Treasury bill rates took a dive in Monday's auction.

Treasury bill rates fell in all maturities following the one percentage-point cut in reserve requirements which took effect last Friday. The benchmark 91-day Treasury bill rate fell to 11.172 percent from 11.679 percent.
"The cut was expected," a dealer said.
The slash in reserve requirements was estimated to have flushed out 6.7 billion pesos from the Central Bank's vaults and pulled down interest rates.
Similarly, the Central Bank dropped its borrowing rates on term reverse repos (RRPs) by 0.25 percentage point each.
The one-month RRPs now fetch a rate of 10.75 percent from 11.0; the two months 10.875 percent from 11.125; and the three months at 11.0 percent from 11.25.
The Central Bank also slashed its borrowing rate on its special series T-bills by 0.425 percentage point each to 10.875 percent from 11.30 percent the previous day.
The Central Bank is currently offering special series T-bills with maturities of 78 and 85 days.
